newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 31.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - From August 1, small companies in areas affected by the floods can ask for advantageous credits. The Industry and Trade Ministry announced yesterday that it will discontinue its other programmes to help small businesses and all funding will be shifted into the programme KREDIT.
- From tomorrow, seven domestic banks, CSOB, Hypobank, IPB, Komercni Banka, Union Banka and Zivnostenska Banka, will begin selling government flood bonds.
- Analysts from CEZ say if the state privatises its electricity transmitting system, it will cause the company losses of more than 25 billion crowns.
- Letov Praha, whose management will propose liquidation in a September general meeting, had losses of 116 million crowns for the first six months of 1997.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Aside from B-prit, Bohemia Sekt and Stock Plzen, which already officially confirmed participation in the tender for Becherovka, a well-informed source also said Unimex will participate. Petr Lukes, who represents Cimex Holding, also entered the tender.
- The price of passenger railway transport will increase by 33 percent from September 1, according to a decision from the Finance Ministry.
- Motoinvest Group, which announced its intention to disband in September, is meeting with the forced administrator of Agrobanka over the future of its stake in the bank.
- Konsolidacni Banka, completely state-owned, had net profits of 202.215 million crowns for the first half of 1997, and its balance sum was 124.559 billion crowns.

PRAVO - Ceska Sporitelna and IPB bank announced further decreases in interest rates on Wednesday. Sporitelna decreased its base rate from 16.6 percent to 15.5 percent. From August 1, IPB will decrease its minimum yearly interest rates by 0.5 percent.
- On Wednesday, builders finished the 61-kilometre D5 highway connecting Plzen to the German border.
- From August 1, all types of pensions -- old-age, full and partial invalid, widow and orphan -- rise by an average of 10.5 percent.
LIDOVE NOVINY - In August, Tchibo Praha will increase the price of its ground coffee by 12 to 15 percent. Its other coffee prices will not change.
- The Prague Stock Exchange received a request from Unipetrol for a listing on the main market.
- The Senate returned a new law on conflicting interests to parliament. The law said that senators and parliament representatives cannot also be in executive positions.
- According to IVVM, 78 percent of Czechs were concerned about the July increase in rents. For 15 percent of citizens, the increase in living expenses is a blow to their family finances.
